# Procter & Gamble (PG) — Quantitative Fundamental Report

**Decision date: 2026-07-17 | Latest filing: 2026-03-31 (Q3 FY2026) | Price as of 2026-07-16: $151.50**

---

## 1. Revenue, Earnings, Margin & Cash-Flow Trajectory

PG's most recent quarter (2026-03-31) delivered revenue of $21.23B and EPS of $1.63. The year-over-year comparison is constructive: revenue grew +7.4% and EPS grew +5.8% versus Q3 2025 (revenue=19.78B, eps=1.54). On an annual basis, this is a solid pace for a mature staples franchise.

However, the sequential trajectory tells a different story. Revenue declined -4.4% quarter-over-quarter from Q2's $22.21B, and EPS dropped -8.4% from $1.78. Tracing the quarterly arc reveals a clear deceleration pattern:

| Quarter | Revenue | EPS |
|---------|---------|-----|
| Q1 FY26 (Sep-25) | $22.39B | $1.95 |
| Q2 FY26 (Dec-25) | $22.21B | $1.78 |
| Q3 FY26 (Mar-26) | $21.23B | $1.63 |

Each successive quarter shows lower revenue and lower EPS. The most recent quarter represents a -5.2% revenue decline and -16.4% EPS decline from Q1. This sequential erosion is meaningful.

**Margin compression is the proximate driver.** The gross margin fell from 51.5% (Q1: $11.50B/$22.39B) to 49.5% (Q3: $10.51B/$21.23B), a 200-basis-point contraction in two quarters. Operating margin compressed more severely: from 26.2% in Q1 ($5.86B) to 21.6% in Q3 ($4.58B). Net margin declined from 21.4% to 18.6% over the same span. Notably, cost of revenue grew faster than revenue on a YoY basis — cost_of_revenue of $10.72B in Q3 FY26 versus $9.69B in Q3 FY25, a +10.6% increase against +7.4% revenue growth — indicating material input-cost pressure.

**Cash generation remains positive but is also weakening sequentially.** Operating cash flow was $4.04B in Q3, down -18.6% from Q2's $4.97B but up +9.2% YoY from $3.71B in Q3 FY25. The quarterly series ($5.41B → $4.97B → $4.04B) mirrors the earnings trajectory. Free cash flow is unavailable in the data; I rely on operating cash flow as the cash-generation proxy.

## 2. Earnings Quality & Balance-Sheet Resilience

Despite margin pressure, several quality metrics remain intact. Net margin at 18.6% and ROE at 29.7% are stable across all observed ratio snapshots (the entire 12-point history from 2025-07 through 2026-07 shows flat net_margin=0.186 and roe=0.297). Gross margin at 51.3% and operating margin at 23.8% (latest ratio data) confirm a structurally profitable business even as the income statement shows sequential weakening.

**The balance sheet is strengthening.** Total equity increased from $52.55B (Mar-25) to $54.73B (Mar-26), a +4.2% improvement. Total liabilities actually declined from $74.05B in Q1 FY26 to $73.65B in Q3, reducing the leverage ratio (total_assets/total_equity) from 2.39x to 2.34x. The equity-to-assets ratio improved from 42.0% to 42.6% over four quarters. This is a clean balance sheet for a consumer staples company — assets of $128.38B are well-supported, and leverage is moderate.

The primary earnings-quality concern is the margin-compression trajectory: cost of revenue is growing at +10.6% YoY against +7.4% revenue growth, implying pricing power is insufficient to offset input-cost inflation. If this gap persists, even the stable trailing profitability ratios will begin to erode.

## 3. Valuation Versus Own History

PG trades at a P/E of 23.8x (2026-07-16), which sits in the **lower half** of its 365-day range of 21.7x–26.3x. The P/B multiple of 7.06x is similarly positioned within its 6.4–7.8x range. By historical standards, current valuation is neither stretched nor deeply discounted — it is mid-range, having compressed from ~24.5x a year ago.

The critical valuation observation: **PG's earnings yield of 4.2% now sits below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.57%.** For a stable-earnings consumer staples company, this is a meaningful headwind. Historically, PG commands a premium because its earnings durability justifies a multiple above the risk-free rate; that rationale weakens when bonds yield more. The P/S ratio of 4.4x and the lack of FCF yield data (fcf_yield=n/a) limit further yield-based comparison, but the earnings-yield-versus-Treasury gap is the dominant valuation signal.

The flat ROE (29.7%) and stable margins provide a floor for valuation — there is no earnings-implosion scenario priced in. But neither is there a compelling discount that offers margin of safety given the sequential deceleration.

## 4. Price Context Versus Fundamental Path

PG closed at $151.50 on 2026-07-16, up +5.7% over the latest quarterly step from $143.38 (2026-04-15). The stock's 365-day range is $137.62–$167.25, placing it 9.4% below the high and 10.1% above the low. The quarterly path shows alternating weakness and recovery: -2.2% (Oct-25 to Jan-26), -0.6% (Jan-26 to Apr-26), then the recent +5.7% bounce.

The price recovery coincides with the Q3 earnings release (filing 2026-04-24), yet Q3 itself showed the weakest sequential results in the available series. This disconnect between price recovery and fundamental deceleration suggests the market may be discounting the margin pressure as transient (possibly oil-related, given the macro context below). If the margin compression proves structural rather than cyclical, the recent price recovery may be premature.

## 5. Macro & Sentiment Overlays

**Macro is mixed but leans supportive for input costs.** WTI crude oil has fallen sharply from ~$110/bbl in late April to $80.03/bbl (2026-07-16), a -12.1% decline over the 90-day lookback. For PG, lower oil means lower petrochemical and packaging input costs. This could provide margin relief in coming quarters — but notably, Q3 (ending March 31) was captured when oil was still elevated (~$91–$108/bbl in the Apr-20 to Apr-24 window), so the full benefit is not yet reflected.

The rate environment remains a valuation overhang. The 10-year yield at 4.57% and 2-year at 4.16% (yield curve spread +0.41%) signal a modestly positive curve but still-elevated absolute rates. The T10Y2Y spread has narrowed from 0.54% to 0.41% over the lookback, suggesting softening growth expectations. Breakeven inflation at 2.22% is well-contained. VIX at 16.73 is below its recent range and benign for defensive equities. The broad dollar index at 120.331 has strengthened modestly, which is a mild headwind for PG's international revenue.

**News sentiment is net positive but thin** (mean score=0.583, 57 articles over 90 days). This is the weakest data input and does not materially alter the fundamental picture.

## 6. Strongest Quantitative Upside & Downside

**Upside case:** YoY growth remains healthy at revenue +7.4%, EPS +5.8%. The balance sheet is improving with declining liabilities. Oil at $80/bbl (down from $110+) should ease input costs, potentially reversing the margin compression in Q4 and beyond. ROE of 29.7% reflects genuine business quality. The P/E at 23.8x is at the lower end of its historical range, offering reversion potential if margins stabilize.

**Downside case:** The sequential deceleration is accelerating — each of the last three quarters shows progressively lower revenue and EPS. Gross margin compressed 200 bps in two quarters (51.5% → 49.5%), and cost of revenue is growing at +10.6% YoY versus +7.4% revenue growth. Operating cash flow declined -18.6% QoQ. The earnings yield (4.2%) no longer compensates for risk relative to risk-free alternatives (10y Treasury = 4.57%). If the margin gap is structural rather than oil-driven, earnings quality deteriorates meaningfully from current levels.

## 7. Provisional Conclusion

PG presents a **cautiously neutral fundamental picture** with a bias toward caution on the near-term trajectory. The business retains high structural quality — stable profitability, strong ROE, improving balance sheet — and the year-over-year growth numbers are respectable for a staples giant. However, the accelerating sequential deceleration in revenue, margins, and cash flow is a genuine yellow flag. The gross-margin compression from 51.5% to 49.5% in two quarters, with cost of revenue growing 3.2 percentage points faster than revenue, suggests pricing power is insufficient in the current environment.

Valuation is fair but not compelling. A 23.8x P/E with a 4.2% earnings yield that now undershoots the 10-year Treasury (4.57%) removes the traditional "quality premium" rationale for owning PG over bonds. The stock is priced for stability, but the fundamentals are showing instability.

The oil-price decline from $110+ to $80 is the key swing factor — if it flows through to lower input costs and restores margins in coming quarters, the deceleration narrative reverses. If margins remain compressed even with cheaper oil, the thesis weakens materially. Pending evidence of margin stabilization, the quantitative fundamentals do not currently justify overweighting PG relative to its own historical valuation-quality profile.

---

# Procter & Gamble (PG) — Qualitative Franchise Assessment

**Decision Date: 2026-07-17 | Analyst: Qualitative Franchise Review**

---

## 1. Business & Franchise Read

P&G is a structurally elite consumer staples franchise. With ~$84–87B in annual revenue across five segments — Fabric & Home Care (35% of sales), Baby/Feminine/Family Care (24%), Beauty (18%), Health Care (14%), and Grooming (9%) — the company operates 60–65+ billion-dollar brands sold in approximately 180 countries. Brands command 10–30% price premiums over private label, supported by ~$8.2B in annual marketing spend and ~$2B in R&D. Return on invested capital runs consistently in the 20–25% range against an estimated WACC of 7–8%, implying meaningful annual economic value creation.

The franchise's durability rests on three pillars: (a) recurring, non-discretionary demand for everyday household and personal care products; (b) unmatched scale-driven distribution — Walmart alone represents ~15% of global sales, with preferential shelf placement and first-call innovation access that newer entrants cannot replicate; and (c) a disciplined capital-allocation machine. Diluted share count has declined from ~3.2B (2010) to ~2.35B (fiscal 2024), a 27% reduction that mechanically amplifies per-share earnings and dividend growth. The 70th consecutive annual dividend increase (reported 2026-07-14) underscores the cash-return identity. Operating margin runs approximately 24%, and the company generates roughly $16B in annual free cash flow.

Innovation remains a differentiator, not a platitude. The Oral-B iO Series ($150–$250 device, generating an estimated $50–$90 in annual recurring brush-head replacement revenue per unit) exemplifies P&G's ability to convert commodity consumables into platform-recurring revenue architectures. E-commerce now represents approximately 17–18% of global net sales and is the fastest-growing channel.

The structural growth runway is defined by emerging-market penetration — India, Sub-Saharan Africa, Southeast Asia, Latin America — where household adoption of premium branded categories remains well below developed-market levels — and by premiumization within existing categories (SK-II, Pampers Premium Protection, Tide evo).

**The structural concern** is volume. Organic sales growth of approximately 4% in fiscal 2024 was driven almost entirely by pricing (~4 percentage points), with volume essentially flat. This raises the question of whether the premium-pricing model has reached a natural boundary where further price increases accelerate private-label adoption without commensurate volume recovery.

---

## 2. Recent Developments

**Q3 FY2026 (reported 2026-04-24):** Organic sales grew 3%, comprising 2% volume growth and 1% pricing — the first quarter showing meaningful volume recovery after a prolonged flat-to-down trend. Beauty led with 7% organic growth; personal care showed high-single-digit gains. Adjusted EPS of $1.59 beat consensus of $1.56, up 3% YoY. The stock rose 1.7% on the print. This is an encouraging signal that the pricing-led to volume-led transition may be underway.

**Q4 FY2026 outlook (earnings due 2026-07-29):** The picture reverses sharply. Analysts project adjusted EPS of ~$1.42, down 4.1% YoY. Revenue estimates center near $21.4B. The compression is driven by a ~$1B after-tax commodity/oil cost headwind concentrated in Q4, tied to Middle East conflict-driven feedstock and logistics disruptions. CFO Andre Schulten quantified the exposure on the Q3 call. Full-year FY2026 guidance points to the low end of the $6.83–$7.09 core EPS range.

**Tariff headwind:** Management has guided a $400M after-tax tariff cost for fiscal 2026, compounding the commodity hit.

**Restructuring:** P&G announced up to 7,000 non-manufacturing job cuts, targeting structural overhead reduction. This carries near-term charges and execution risk but is designed to fund the productivity reinvestment cycle.

**Dividend (2026-07-14):** The 70th consecutive annual increase places P&G above the Dividend King threshold. Current yield: 2.9%, annual dividend: $4.26/share.

**Stock performance:** PG has declined ~16% from its highs and ~5% over the trailing 52 weeks, lagging the S&P 500's +20.3% return and even the Consumer Staples ETF's +3.9% gain. The current P/E of approximately 22x sits at a discount to historical norms when the business was performing at full strength.

**Forward trajectory:** Analyst consensus carries normalized EPS to ~$6.89 for FY2026 (essentially flat vs FY2025) and projects ~$7.05 for FY2027 (+2.3%). However, the quarterly trajectory is more informative: a 4% YoY EPS decline in Q4, followed by estimated reacceleration to 8% growth by June 2027. The July 29 print is the inflection point — it will clarify whether the trough is priced or deeper.

---

## 3. Material Risks & Offsets

**Risks:**
- **Volume stagnation and private-label encroachment.** Organic growth has been pricing-dependent. Private label is gaining ground in diapers, bathroom tissue, and laundry — categories where brand differentiation is harder to sustain. Gillette's share losses have proven "sticky." This is the single most important structural risk to the franchise premium.
- **Commodity/tariff cost shock.** The combined ~$1.4B after-tax headwind (tariffs + oil/commodity) in FY2026 is compressing margins and may persist into FY2026 if Middle East tensions continue. Gross margin compressed 100bps last quarter.
- **China deterioration.** Greater China has shrunk from 12% to ~9% of sales, driven by consumer weakness and SK-II boycotts. Recovery timing is uncertain.
- **FX structural exposure.** ~49% of revenue is generated outside North America across ~70 countries, creating persistent translation and transaction headwinds.
- **Tariff audit/compliance risk.** P&G's extensive cross-border supply chain faces increasingly complex customs scrutiny and penalty exposure, adding a structural cost layer that was previously immaterial.
- **Restructuring execution.** 7,000 job cuts paired with near-term charges and a referenced CEO transition introduce operational risk.

**Offsets:**
- **Q3 volume recovery.** 2% volume growth in Q3 FY2026, after prolonged flat-to-down trends, suggests the cycle may be turning. If sustained, this would materially weaken the bear case on private-label erosion.
- **Productivity reinvestment cycle.** P&G targets $1.5B in annual cost savings through manufacturing and supply-chain efficiency, reinvested into brand building rather than dropped to earnings. This funds the innovation/marketing intensity without external capital.
- **Valuation reset.** The ~22x P/E, at a discount to historical norms, appears to price in the trough quarter and near-term headwinds. If EPS reaccelerates to 8% growth as projected by June 2027, the multiple has room to recover.
- **Defensive cash generation.** ~$16B annual FCF, $15B planned shareholder returns in FY2026, and the 70-year dividend streak provide downside support and capital-return optionality.

---

## 4. Qualitative Assessment

**Neutral-to-positive on fundamental attractiveness.**

P&G is a structurally superior franchise: category-leading brands in essential consumer goods, 187 years of continuous presence, ~$84–87B in recurring revenue, 20–25% ROIC, and a capital-return discipline unmatched in the sector. The brand moat is deep and real.

The near-term narrative is undeniably pressured — a ~$1.4B cost headwind, margin compression, volume stagnation, and private-label gains in key categories. But these pressures appear cyclical rather than structural. The Q3 FY2026 volume recovery (2% volume growth) is the most important qualitative data point: if sustained, it would demonstrate that the pricing-for-volume transition is achievable and that private-label gains are reversible when P&G reinvests in product superiority.

The 16% drawdown and ~22x P/E appear to discount much of the near-term pain. The July 29 earnings report is the key near-term catalyst — it will clarify whether the Q4 commodity hit was as guided or worse, and whether management's fiscal 2027 tone supports the projected EPS reacceleration.

The principal risk is that private-label momentum in diapers, tissue, and laundry proves more durable than the franchise model assumes, permanently compressing the pricing premium and shifting P&G from a growth compounder to a low-growth income stock. That would warrant a structurally lower multiple. Current evidence does not yet support that conclusion, but it bears close monitoring.

---
